preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of initial roads m is between 0 and n-1 inclusive.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in initial_roads)
preconditions.description: Each initial road connects two distinct cities within the valid range.
The number of initial road definitions matches m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n for x in query_cities)
preconditions.description: All city indices referenced in queries are within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(type == 1 or (type == 2 and len(args) == 2) for type, args in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query is either type 1 with one city argument or type 2 with two city arguments.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == sum(1 for t, _ in queries if t == 1)
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of type 1 queries.

postconditions.expression: all(int(line) == diameter_of_region_at_query_time(i) for i, line in enumerate(output_lines) if queries[i][0] == 1)
postconditions.description: For each type 1 query, the output line contains the integer length of the longest path (diameter) in the region containing the specified city at that moment in time.

postconditions.expression: all(merged_diameter(i) == min_possible_diameter_after_merge(i) for i in range(len(queries)) if queries[i][0] == 2)
postconditions.description: For each type 2 query, the merge operation connects the two regions such that the resulting region's diameter is minimized among all possible single-edge connections between the two regions.
